honesty: FIEZEL does not predict IELTS bands or TOEFL scores. The audio is generated via text-to-speech from original scripts, not actual exam recordings: one voice for all speakers, and without the variety of accents used in real exams. What is practiced here is question format, listening under pressure, and note-taking - not accent familiarization.

ielts_listening_s1.label: IELTS Listening Section 1
ielts_listening_s1.note: Everyday conversation, usually form-filling. Audio is played ONCE. You may read the questions while listening - that is how the exam works, and that is the skill itself: reading, listening, and writing simultaneously.

ielts_listening_s2.label: IELTS Listening Section 2
ielts_listening_s2.note: Monologue about everyday situations. Audio ONCE. Original map/plan questions require images, so here they are replaced by location-based multiple-choice questions - that is an adaptation, not the full format.

ielts_listening_s3.label: IELTS Listening Section 3
ielts_listening_s3.note: Academic discussion between two to four people. Audio ONCE. What is tested: following who thinks what, not just capturing facts.

ielts_listening_s4.label: IELTS Listening Section 4
ielts_listening_s4.note: Academic lecture without pauses. Audio ONCE and does not stop in the middle - it is the hardest part precisely because of that.

toefl_listening_conversation.label: TOEFL iBT Listening - Conversation
toefl_listening_conversation.note: Campus conversation. Audio ONCE, and questions only appear AFTER the audio finishes - so note-taking is not an option, but a necessity.

toefl_listening_lecture.label: TOEFL iBT Listening - Lecture
toefl_listening_lecture.note: Academic lecture. Audio ONCE, questions appear afterwards. The question types test the lecturer's structure and intent, not just the content.

lx-s1-1.explain: Spelled out directly by him: M-A-R-S-H.

lx-s1-2.explain: "Forty-two Bridgeway Road." In the actual exam, numbers are written as digits.

lx-s1-3.explain: "L S nine, four T P." Postcodes are always read letter by letter - write them together without hesitation.

lx-s1-4.explain: "Oh-seven-nine, one-one, three-four-oh, six-two-eight." The officer repeats - that repetition is provided by the exam for correction purposes.

lx-s1-5.explain: He can swim but his technique is poor and he gets tired after two laps - that is the definition of 'Improvers' given by the officer.

lx-s1-6.explain: He chooses Thursday because on Tuesday he only finishes work at seven.

lx-s1-7.explain: One session per week = 32 pounds a month. The trap here is 48, which is for TWO sessions.

lx-s1-8.explain: One-time payment fee of 15 pounds; he cannot get an exemption because he is neither a student nor over 65.

lx-s1-9.explain: "We don't supply padlocks any more." Goggles are only optional - that is the differentiator.

lx-s2-1.explain: "The large building on the western edge." The Rose Garden is on the eastern side.

lx-s2-2.explain: Only the upper path is closed, because the metal becomes slippery - not the entire Glasshouse.

lx-s2-3.explain: "On your left as you're walking up" - and he is walking north, so left = northwest. The toilets are in the same building.

lx-s2-4.explain: There is a weight limit, and the rule is a maximum of fifteen children at a time.

lx-s2-5.explain: The reason is stated directly: there is no lighting.

lx-s2-6.explain: "It's absolutely fine to say so. What is not fine is guessing." The berry example is used to emphasize this.

lx-s3-1.explain: Initially they thought it was the effect of the trees - but the difference remained at three in the morning, so it was not shade.

lx-s3-2.explain: Priya discards items, while Tom keeps and marks them - don't mix them up.

lx-s3-3.explain: Two reasons, and both must be captured - the number of sensors AND the fact that the data values are of different types.

lx-s3-4.explain: "The failure mode here isn't dropping data or keeping it. It's doing either quietly."

lx-s3-5.explain: Three meters versus two meters, and the difference was measured primarily over paved surfaces.

lx-s3-6.explain: "A wide honest interval is worth more than a narrow invented one."

lx-s3-7.explain: The tutor distinguishes between audiences: Priya's order is suitable for a conference, Tom's order is for a graded report.

lx-s3-8.explain: The laboratory is closed for maintenance on the 9th and 10th, while the deadline is the 12th.

lx-s4-1.explain: The difference is about ten minutes - and it was never a problem as long as the fastest communication was as fast as a horse.

lx-s4-2.explain: Great Western Railway. Passengers in the west of England had to subtract the difference themselves.

lx-s4-3.explain: Late passengers are troublesome; two trains on one track with crews who disagree on the time leads to a collision.

lx-s4-4.explain: The practical standard had been used by trains since the 1850s; the law followed in 1880.

lx-s4-5.explain: The defendant arrived on time according to local time - he was correct according to the old rules, and that is precisely what worked against him.

lx-s4-6.explain: And the choice was about shipping, not scientific superiority: the majority of world maps already used Greenwich.

lx-s4-7.explain: "What I want you to take from this is not the dates. It is the shape of the process."

lx-tc-1.explain: Gist-purpose questions ask for the REASON for coming, not the most interesting thing that appears later.

lx-tc-2.explain: The book is available at three libraries - the problem is time, not availability.

lx-tc-3.explain: That is why he must choose one essay first and request the second one next month.

lx-tc-4.explain: The large book is registered under the donor's name, not the subject - so any search will not find it.

lx-tc-5.explain: Cannot leave the building, pencils only, photography allowed without flash.

lx-tc-6.explain: That expression means using two safeguards at once - he suggests still requesting a scan as a backup.

lx-toefl-lecture.title: Kuliah biologi: warna peringatan dan peniruan

lx-tl-1.explain: Camouflage and Bates' history are only touched upon; the backbone of the lecture is those three mechanisms.

lx-tl-2.explain: The entire system depends on the predator surviving and then REMEMBERING - that is why the color is not a warning to the attacker at that moment.

lx-tl-3.explain: There is a natural ceiling: mimics are only safe as long as their numbers remain small compared to the poisonous ones.

lx-tl-4.explain: The teaching cost is shared - and no one is freeloading, both benefit equally.

lx-tl-5.explain: Every lesson is paid for with an individual's life; one lesson for two species means fewer victims.

lx-tl-6.explain: The lecturer concludes by asking students to be ready to DEBATE the continuum claim - a sign it has not been agreed upon.

lx-s2v2-1.explain: "You can bring two guests with you each month at half price." Not free - half price.

lx-s2v2-2.explain: "At the back of the building, behind the stairs" - the only room where items can actually be touched.

lx-s2v2-3.explain: The second floor is staff-only - do not go up; ask at the front desk, and a viewing is arranged in about two weeks.

lx-s2v2-4.explain: "Beside the cloakroom, on the right as you come in." The coin is returned when the locker is opened again.

lx-s2v2-5.explain: The first Tuesday of every month opens at one in the afternoon because the gallery is cleaned in the morning. The trap: the one closed all day is Monday.

lx-s2v2-6.explain: "Your membership card is yours and nobody else's." Loan cards will be held at the front desk.

lx-ielts-s4-v2.title: Kuliah: kina dan monopoli obat malaria

lx-s4v2-1.explain: "The bark of the cinchona tree" - the medicine is taken from the bark, not the leaves or roots.

lx-s4v2-2.explain: "Not because the trees died, but because they lived." The trees were fertile - their quinine content was nearly zero.

lx-s4v2-3.explain: "The turning point came in eighteen sixty-five." On the answer sheet, write 1865.

lx-s4v2-4.explain: England rejected the seeds—"one savours the irony"—so Ledger sold them cheaply to the Netherlands.

lx-s4v2-5.explain: The digression shows that the Quechua name from the Andes crossed over along with the tree - "languages, like bark, preserve things".

lx-s4v2-6.explain: "Roughly ninety percent" - ninety percent of the world's supply from the highlands of one island.

lx-s4v2-7.explain: "Synthetic substitutes had been developed and manufactured at scale" — permanently ending the quinine monopoly.

lx-s4v2-8.explain: "Carry the shape of the argument" - concentration looks like strength until the day it becomes the mechanism of its own collapse.
